response_contract: Return only the requested JSON object. Do not add prose or markdown.

cases.prompt: Use east as +x and north as +y. A copper key starts at (2,-1). A jade coin is three units west and two units north of the key. A red bead is one unit east of the coin. A glass ring is four units south of the bead. Return the coordinates and the compass direction from the ring to the key as {"key":[x,y],"coin":[x,y],"bead":[x,y],"ring":[x,y],"ring_to_key":"direction"}.

Use east as +x and north as +y. Elm is at (-4,7). Fir is five units east and three units south of Elm. Ash is two units west of Fir. Yew is six units north of Ash. Return {"elm":[x,y],"fir":[x,y],"ash":[x,y],"yew":[x,y],"elm_to_yew":"direction"}.

Ivo starts at (0,0) facing south. A left turn is relative to the current heading. He turns left, walks five steps, turns around, walks two steps, then turns right and walks three steps. Return {"position":[x,y],"facing":"direction"} using east as +x and north as +y.

Mira starts at (6,-2) facing west. She walks four, turns right, walks seven, turns right, walks one, turns around, walks three, then turns left and walks two. Return {"position":[x,y],"facing":"direction"} using east as +x and north as +y.

A robot maps local coordinates to world coordinates by (u,v) -> (v+4,-u+1). Map local (-2,5), then apply the world displacement (-3,+2), then invert the mapping. Return {"mapped_world":[x,y],"final_world":[x,y],"final_local":[u,v]}.

A map converts local (u,v) to world (x,y) by x=2u-v+3 and y=u+v-4. Convert local (5,-2), apply world displacement (-4,+7), and solve for the resulting local coordinate. Return {"mapped_world":[x,y],"final_world":[x,y],"final_local":[u,v]}.

Minecraft frame convention: local +x is right, local +y is up, and local +z is forward. A frame at world origin (12,64,-7) faces east, so local (x,y,z) maps to world (origin.x+z, origin.y+y, origin.z+x). Map local point (-3,5,8). Return {"world":[x,y,z]}.

Track distinct objects. Red starts at (1,2), Blue at (-3,5), and Green at (4,-1). Apply in order: move Red by (+2,-4); swap the complete positions of Blue and Green; move the object now at (-3,5) by (-1,+6); move Blue by (+5,+1). Return {"red":[x,y],"blue":[x,y],"green":[x,y]}.

Track three drones. A starts at (0,0,0), B at (8,-2,4), C at (-5,3,1). Apply in order: A += (2,1,-3); C += (4,-2,6); swap all coordinates of A and B; B += (-1,5,2). Return {"A":[x,y,z],"B":[x,y,z],"C":[x,y,z]}.

Crate A contains boxes B and C. B contains gems D and E. C contains box F. F contains gem G. The left-to-right shelf order is E, H, D, G. Return {"direct_container_of_G":"name","outermost_container_of_G":"name","left_of_D":"name","between_E_and_G":["name","name"]}.
